title: Valuative uniqueness implies separatedness for quasi-separated algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $g:Y\to Z$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose the diagonal $\Delta_g:Y\to Y\times_ZY$ is quasi-compact. Suppose also that for every valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$ [def-trf-valuation-ring] and every $z:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Z$, any two lifts $a,b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$ over $z$ with $a|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}=b|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$ are equal. Then $g$ is separated: its diagonal is a closed immersion, meaning that each scheme base change of the representable diagonal is a closed immersion of schemes.

proof.text: Put $P=Y\times_ZY$ and let $\Delta:Y\to P$ be the diagonal. The fibre product exists as an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Fix a valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$, write $j:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and consider a square $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$, $v:\operatorname{Spec}R\to P$ with $\Delta u=vj$. Write $a=p_1v$, $b=p_2v$. By the fibre-product equations $ga=gb$, and the two projections of $\Delta u=vj$ give $aj=u=bj$. The hypothesis on $g$ therefore gives $a=b$. The map $a$ extends $u$ and satisfies $\Delta a=v$: their first components are $a$ and their second components are $a=b$, so the fibre-product universal property gives the equality. Thus every valuation square for $\Delta$ has a lift already over $R$.

The hypothesis makes $\Delta$ quasi-compact. Step 1 verifies the valuative existence hypothesis of [lem-sfb-space-qc-valuative-existence-closed], taking the identity field extension $K\subset K$ and the same dominating valuation ring $R$. Apply that node to the morphism $\Delta:Y\to P$ of algebraic spaces. It follows that $\Delta$ is universally closed.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-separated-diagonal-closed] to $g:Y\to Z$. Its universally closed diagonal, proved in step 2, is a closed immersion. In the cited statement this means a representable map whose every scheme base change is a closed immersion of schemes, exactly the conclusion required here.
